text.p: Hotel operator AAPC Ltd said on Monday it would restructure its Asian operations to boost performance and take advantage of the next stage of the hotel and tourism cycle in Asia.

Features of the restructuring included a review of costs and assets so as to maximise returns from the renewed focus on core business activities, a rationalisation of regional offices in Asia and the relocation of key personnel to Singapore.
"The principal aim of the reorganisation is to make our operation in Asia more focussed and efficient," chairman David Baffsky said in a statement, noting the intensified Asian focus.

"We are entering a new phase of development which requires a greater concentration of resources in Asia to support the large number of additional hotels that will join the network up to and beyond the year 2000," Baffsky said.

As part of the restructure, group managing director Raymond Capdevila will relocate to Singapore working with newly appointed Asian managing director, Tony Young, who has previous experience in the Asian region with Southern Pacific Hotels.

AAPC currently operates 131 hotels in the Asia Pacific region with another scheduled to joinn the network in the next two years. The company's major brands are Sofitel, Novotel, Mercure Ibis and Formule 1.
AAPC is 24.4 percent owned by French hotel group Accor SA .
AAPC shares ended a cent lower at A$0.78 on turnover of 647,735 shares.
